concepts.name: Graph Terminology
concepts.mental_model: Google Maps road network: intersections = vertices, roads = edges; one-way streets = directed, distances = weights.
concepts.mnemonic: Mark before you walk - a visited set is the seatbelt that stops cycles from looping you forever.

concepts.name: Graph Representations
concepts.mental_model: Adjacency list = your phone contacts (only the people you actually know). Adjacency matrix = a V x V seating grid with a cell reserved for every possible pair.
concepts.mnemonic: List = Lean (sparse), Matrix = Massive (dense). Matrix size = V^2 always; edges never shrink it. | THE CURRENCY: List = pay per FRIEND (degree). Matrix = pay per SEAT in the row (V). Matrix's one superpower: edge u-v? in O(1).

past_mistakes.note: Sized the adjacency matrix by edge count (~30M) instead of V^2. A matrix is ALWAYS V^2 regardless of edges: 10M nodes = 100 trillion cells, even with zero edges. Also wrongly called matrix neighbor-traversal 'constant' - iterating one node's neighbors in a matrix is O(V), worse than the list's O(degree). [Re-tested 2026-07-04 quiz: PASSED - said V^2 immediately.]

Python dict key-type bug: pre-initialized isolated nodes with str(i) keys but edges used int labels, so adj[1] and adj['1'] became separate keys (1 == '1' is False). Got conceptual isolated-node fix right but mismatched key types. Remember: to a dict, 1 and '1' are different keys.

2026-07-17 quiz: the OLD matrix mistake wearing the other shoe - priced adjacency-LIST operations in V (said neighbor-iteration and edge-query cost O(99999)) when the list's currency is DEGREE: both are O(degree(u)), ~4 avg in a V=100k/E=200k graph. The list exists precisely to avoid the matrix's O(V) row-scan. Corrected via phone-contacts anchor + 'pay per friend vs pay per seat'. Retested with celebrity node c (degree 99,999) vs normal node (degree 4): PASSED - correctly priced both in degree, seeing that degree can coincidentally equal V-1. concepts.name: Breadth-First Search
concepts.mental_model: A wave/ripple spreading from a stone dropped in water: reaches everything 1 hop away, THEN everything 2 hops away, never skipping ahead. WHY first-arrival = shortest: the queue is SORTED by distance - it only ever holds ring d and ring d+1, in that order (monotone-queue invariant). Ring-(d+1) nodes are only let into line by ring-d nodes, so nothing farther can jump the line.
concepts.mnemonic: Breadth = Queue, fan out in rings (FIFO). Depth = Stack, dive down (LIFO). Swap them and BFS becomes DFS. And: mark visited on ENQUEUE, not dequeue. | FIFO keeps the wave SORTED - the queue never goes backwards in distance.

past_mistakes.note: Said to mark a node visited when DEQUEUED. Wrong: that lets the same node be enqueued multiple times (diamond graph A-B,A-C,B-D,C-D enqueues D twice). Correct idiom: mark visited the instant you ENQUEUE, so each node enters the queue exactly once. [Re-tested 2026-07-04 quiz: PASSED with nuance - led with ENQUEUE and correctly noted dequeue works too with a skip-guard but floods the queue; transferred the DFS push-vs-pop insight to BFS.]
Watch transfer: used distances[node] + 6 (HackerRank's per-edge weight). Generic BFS hop-distance is + 1. Same algorithm, different per-edge cost.

concepts.name: Depth-First Search
concepts.mental_model: Maze walk: take the first unexplored corridor, go deep until a dead end, then backtrack to the most recent junction with an unexplored corridor. (vs BFS's spreading wave.)
concepts.mnemonic: Depth = Stack (dive down, LIFO). In recursion the CALL STACK is your stack. At a dead end, back up to the last node with an unexplored neighbor. And: mark BEFORE you recurse, never after.

past_mistakes.note: Used `global dfs_order, visited` in recursive DFS - unnecessary. A nested helper only mutates (append/add), never rebinds, so the closure shares them without global/nonlocal. global just leaks module names (smell).

Iterative-DFS nuance to retain: LIFO flips neighbor order, so an explicit-stack DFS dives into the LAST-listed neighbor first; push reversed() to mirror recursion. Two valid marking strategies: mark-on-PUSH (each node once, no stack dups - what they used) vs mark-on-POP + skip-if-visited guard (mirrors recursion, allows dups). Recursive DFS dies past Python's ~1000 recursion limit; iterative does not.

concepts.name: Traversal Patterns (trees/graphs/grids)
concepts.mental_model: ONE engine, TWO knobs. BFS/DFS never change; across tree/graph/grid only (1) the neighbor function and (2) whether you need visited change. Tree: neighbors=children, no visited. Graph: neighbors=adj[node], need visited. Grid: neighbors=4 dirs+bounds check, mark in-place. Matrix: neighbors = all j where isConnected[i][j]==1, need visited set.
concepts.mnemonic: Same engine, two knobs: NEIGHBORS + VISITED. Shortest/levels -> BFS; explore-all/paths/components/cycle -> DFS. | Comprehension order: [WHAT for VAR in WHERE if CONDITION] - WHAT first, it's the append() yanked to the front. | e-NUM-erate: the NUMber comes first - (index, value), like '1. eggs'. | Self-loop lives on the DIAGONAL M[i][i] - the node staring at its own reflection.

past_mistakes.note: Matrix row vs neighbor list (recurring, echoes Graph Representations): initially said 'neighbors of i = isConnected[i]'. But isConnected[i] is the whole ROW of 0/1s; the neighbors are the indices j where isConnected[i][j]==1 and j!=i (an O(V) row-scan). Corrected and CONFIRMED live on a concrete 3x3 matrix (neighbors of 0 = {1}). Re-pull in a quiz.

concepts.name: Connected Components
concepts.mental_model: Islands in an ocean: each maximal group of mutually-reachable nodes is one island. Count islands by walking each unvisited node and flood-filling its whole island with BFS/DFS.
concepts.mnemonic: Outer loop = find dry land; inner traversal = flood the whole island. Count++ per fresh island.

concepts.name: Cycle Detection
concepts.mental_model: TWO axes of visited, not one. Plain traversal = 1 axis (seen?) which only guarantees TERMINATION. Cycle detection adds a 2nd axis (still on my current path?). Directed graph: 3 colors - WHITE unseen, GRAY in-progress/on the DFS recursion stack, BLACK fully done. A cycle EXISTS iff DFS finds an edge to a GRAY node (a back edge). Edge to BLACK = harmless convergence, not a cycle. (Undirected variant: plain visited + parent check.) | UNIFYING FRAMEWORK (the deep one): a cycle == a BACK EDGE and nothing else (edge back to an ancestor still on the DFS stack/gray). Both directed & undirected detect the same thing. DFS edge classification by neighbor color: WHITE = tree edge (recurse), GRAY = back edge (CYCLE), BLACK = forward/cross edge (NOT a cycle). KEY FACT: undirected DFS has NO cross/forward (black-row) edges - two-way streets forbid them (if u-v and neither is the other's ancestor, the earlier-entered one would have descended the two-way edge -> contradiction). So undirected: every visited non-parent neighbor is a back edge -> only need visited+parent. Directed: edges to BLACK nodes (forward/cross) are visited-but-not-ancestors = not cycles -> must separate gray from black.
concepts.mnemonic: Gray = on the stove; point back to gray and the snake eats its own tail = CYCLE. Black is served and safe. Plain visited STOPS loops; the gray axis DETECTS them. | DIRECTED vs UNDIRECTED = one-way vs two-way streets: 'STACK vs DOOR'. Directed watches the STACK (cycle = edge to GRAY; 3 colors; NO parent - A<->B is a real 2-cycle). Undirected watches the DOOR (cycle = a visited neighbor that isn't your PARENT; 2 states; NO gray/black). Gray for one-way, Parent for two-way. | U-TURN vs ROUNDABOUT: one two-way road walked back = U-turn (ONE edge, innocent - that's what parent-skip skips). Two one-way roads back = roundabout (TWO distinct edges, real 2-cycle - that's why directed must NOT skip the parent).

past_mistakes.note: Conflated the two jobs of 'visited': assumed visited alone detects cycles. Untangled it - plain 2-state visited only prevents infinite loops (termination) by refusing to re-recurse; it CANNOT tell whether a re-seen node is still on the current path (cycle) vs already finished (convergence) because it lacks that 2nd axis. Resolved cleanly; learner named it 'axis of information'. [Re-tested 2026-07-17 quiz Q1: PASSED - articulated termination-vs-detection and the ON_STACK third state unprompted; only needed the word 'convergence' supplied for the black case.]

Got genuinely confused on WHY directed vs undirected cycle detection differ. Built intuition via ONE-WAY vs TWO-WAY streets: directed one-way -> an edge to a FINISHED (black) node can't loop back, so you MUST distinguish gray(open) vs black(closed), and parent is irrelevant (A->B + B->A is a real 2-cycle); undirected two-way -> any visited non-parent neighbor guarantees a loop (no cross edges in undirected DFS), so track PARENT only, no black needed. Contrast anchor: an extra edge to a seen node is innocent when directed (lands on black) but forms a triangle=cycle when undirected. Mnemonic banked: STACK vs DOOR.

Self-contradiction surfaced: they correctly said parent-skip exists to avoid re-walking the came-from edge - but if the U-turn were a real cycle, parent-skip would be a BUG not a feature. concepts.name: Union-Find (DSU)
concepts.mental_model: LEARNER'S OWN VOCABULARY (always use it): GROUPS and LEADERS, not islands/labels. Naive scheme: every member stores their leader directly -> same-group check is O(1), but a merge must relabel the entire losing group. DSU scheme: members store only their immediate BOSS (parent pointer, org-chart chain); the leader is whoever is their own boss. find = climb the boss chain; union = the losing leader gets a new boss.
concepts.mnemonic: THE LOSER PAYS - so make the SMALL group lose (small joins large). Cycle test: an edge inside one group is redundant - same leader twice = cycle. | Lazy unions build a CONGA LINE (skewed-BST disease: find O(n)). Fix 1 small-joins-large: depth grows only by LOSING, losing DOUBLES your group -> height <= log2 n. Fix 2 path compression: climb once, everyone met gets the leader's SPEED DIAL. Together ~O(1) amortized (inverse Ackermann <= 5). | SUBTLETY: union links the two LEADERS, never the edge's endpoints.

Insidious - correct whenever the loser is a singleton; first diverged on (3,4) (loser {4,5} = 2 members): size[find(1)] printed 4 (= 1 + wins, counting VICTORIES) not 5 (members). Anchor: 'the merger acquired the company but only put the CEO on payroll' - absorb the ROSTER. NOTE: bug was TOLD on request (learner declined to run/trace) - re-test this cold: give a stream where the loser is bigger than 1 and ask what += 1 would print.

concepts.name: Topological Sort
concepts.mental_model: A LINEUP, not a WALK. Lay every node on a line left-to-right; the order is valid iff EVERY edge points rightward. Consecutive nodes need NOT be adjacent (A,B,C,D is valid for A->C,B->C,C->D even though A->B is not an edge; two disconnected nodes X,Y have a topo order but no path). Getting dressed: socks before shoes, pants before belt - the output is the single sequence you put every garment on in, and unrelated garments (socks vs shirt) still both appear. KAHN'S: in-degree = your WAIT COUNT, how many people you are still waiting on; 0 = free to walk. Place a node -> everyone waiting on it crosses a name off; a node joins the ready pool only when its LAST blocker leaves.
concepts.mnemonic: A topological order is a LINEUP, not a WALK - every arrow points RIGHT. | Your in-degree is your WAIT COUNT; zero = free to go. | SHORT LINEUP = CYCLE: if len(order) < n when the pool runs dry, the leftovers are all waiting on each other = deadlock. One integer comparison gives you LC 207 for free. | The pool can be a queue, stack, anything - the container only picks WHICH valid order you get, not whether it is valid.

concepts.name: Minimum Spanning Tree
concepts.mental_model: City planner with a price-sorted menu of roads: go top-down, build a road only if it connects two towns that can't already reach each other; a road between already-connected towns only makes a loop. Kruskal grows a FOREST whose groups fuse (bridge edges), not one tree.
concepts.mnemonic: Sort the menu. Union is the bouncer. Close at n-1. (= edges.sort by weight; loop body is `if uf.union(u,v):` keep; break when len(mst)==n-1). | REDUNDANT beats CHEAP: an edge inside one group is bounced no matter its price.
